input: Get a professional financial plan consultation

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Financial planning covers many domains (retirement, investments, debt, taxes, estate, budgeting) — knowing which areas to focus on shapes who to hire and what to prepare.
Whether this is for an individual, a couple, or a family changes what documents are needed and what kind of advisor is appropriate.
The user's current life stage or triggering event (new job, marriage, inheritance, approaching retirement) determines the urgency and specific focus of the consultation.
Budget for the consultation itself (free intro session, fee-only planner, AUM-based advisor) narrows down which type of professional is accessible.
Whether the user prefers in-person, virtual, or a specific type of advisor (fiduciary, robo-advisor, bank-affiliated) affects where to search and who to contact.
Knowing whether the user has already started researching advisors or is starting from scratch determines the immediate first action in the plan.
The user's definition of a successful consultation (a written financial plan, investment strategy, debt payoff roadmap) sets the standard for choosing the right advisor and evaluating the outcome.

gold.taskTitle: Get a professional financial plan consultation
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to meet with a professional financial advisor or planner to receive expert guidance on their financial situation.

questions.title: Which financial topics does this consultation need to cover?
questions.description: Identify the primary focus areas — such as retirement planning, investing, debt management, tax strategy, budgeting, or estate planning — to find the right specialist.

questions.title: Is this plan for you alone, a partner, or a family?
questions.description: Determine who the consultation is for, as this affects the type of advisor needed and the documents or financial data that must be gathered beforehand.

questions.title: What life event or situation is prompting this consultation now?
questions.description: Understand the triggering context — such as a new job, upcoming retirement, major purchase, or general financial check-up — to set the right urgency and framing.

questions.title: What is your budget for the advisor's consultation fee?
questions.description: Clarify how much the user is willing to spend, since advisors range from free introductory sessions to fee-only planners charging hundreds of dollars per hour.

questions.title: Do you prefer to meet in person or would virtual work?
questions.description: Establish the user's preference for meeting format, which directly affects which advisors and platforms are worth pursuing.

questions.title: Have you already identified any specific advisors or firms?
questions.description: Find out whether the user is starting from scratch or has already done some research, so the plan can begin at the right step.

questions.title: What would a successful outcome from this consultation look like?
questions.description: Define what 'done well' means — whether that is a written financial plan, a clear investment strategy, a debt payoff roadmap, or simply actionable next steps.
